summary:
Sol Survivor is an interactive, browser-based Mars survival and astronaut training game designed for children aged 7–12. Developed using Phaser 4, TypeScript and Vite, it places players in the role of junior astronauts tasked with establishing and maintaining a sustainable Mars outpost. Players customize their astronauts, explore Jezero Crater or Arcadia Planitia, manage life-support systems, operate a rover, and complete five progressive Sol missions involving radiation protection, scientific exploration, resource production and emergency survival.

The project addresses NASA's Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer challenge by transforming complex space exploration concepts into an engaging, hands-on learning experience. It incorporates NASA resources, including DONKI space-weather information, Mars environmental reference data and real Martian terrain imagery, connecting gameplay with planetary science. Through exploration, problem-solving and resource management, Astra Nexus helps young learners understand the challenges of human missions to Mars while inspiring curiosity about STEM and the future of space exploration.
details:
🚀 Sol Survivor

Sol Survivor is a browser-based Mars survival simulation that places players in the role of junior astronauts preparing humanity for life on another planet. Through an interactive mission environment, players experience the scientific, engineering and survival challenges associated with establishing a sustainable human presence on Mars.

The journey begins with astronaut customization, followed by the selection of a landing site—Jezero Crater or Arcadia Planitia—and the construction of a Martian outpost. Players can explore the Martian landscape, operate rovers, investigate scientific locations and interact with essential habitat systems.

Across five progressive Sol missions, players encounter challenges involving life-support management, radiation protection, Martian soil hazards, subsurface water-ice exploration, resource production and emergency habitat repairs. Every decision matter, as players must balance oxygen, water, power, crew health and habitat safety to keep their mission operational.

💻 Technology Stack
  • Game Engine: Phaser 4.2.1
  • Programming Languages: TypeScript, JavaScript
  • Frontend / Build Tools: Vite, HTML5, CSS
  • Backend: Node.js and Express-based services
  • NASA Data Integration: NASA DONKI and Mars environmental data services
  • Planetary Mapping: NASA Mars Trek terrain imagery
  • Development Environment: Visual Studio Code
  • Version Control: Git and GitHub
  • Deployment: Browser-based web deployment
🌟 Innovation Highlights

🧑‍🚀 Astronaut Customization: Players create their own astronaut identity before beginning their Mars mission.

🪐 Martian Landing Site Selection: Choose between Jezero Crater and Arcadia Planitia, introducing players to real Martian geographical locations.

🏠 Interactive Mars Outpost: Explore and operate habitat systems, including the greenhouse, power switchboard and radiation protection systems.

📡 NASA-Inspired Space Science: Connect gameplay with NASA space-weather information, Mars environmental references and real Martian terrain imagery.

🔋 Survival and Resource Management: Balance oxygen, water, power and crew health while maintaining a sustainable habitat.

🚙 Rover Exploration: Travel across the Martian landscape to investigate scientific locations and explore subsurface water-ice resources.

🛠️ Five Progressive Sol Missions: Experience increasingly challenging scientific, engineering and survival scenarios, including emergency habitat repairs.

🎮 Learning Through Gameplay: Understand planetary science and space engineering through interactive challenges instead of relying on static lessons or quizzes.

🎯 Intended Impact

Sol Survivor aims to make planetary exploration accessible and exciting for young learners. By introducing concepts such as life-support engineering, radiation protection, in-situ resource utilization (ISRU), planetary geology and sustainable habitat design, the game encourages scientific curiosity, critical thinking and problem-solving.

The ultimate goal is to inspire children to see themselves as future scientists, engineers and space explorers.
